title: Ops Recipe Packager: DSL & Runtime for Admin Utilities
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: On-call and first-line support repeatedly author ad-hoc scripts and runbooks; we lack a compact, typed packaging format that is safe to execute from the Console or operator CLI. Goal: build an 'Ops Recipe Packager'—a small declarative DSL and runtime that compiles human-friendly admin steps into sandboxed, auditable tasks. The packager should make it easy to convert existing runbook steps into parameterized recipes, enable safe dry-run mode, attach telemetry hooks, and expose a single API surface so Console and CLI can render interactive shortflows without shipping bespoke code per recipe. Must integrate with RBAC and audit logs and support canary rollout of recipes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) DSL prototype accepts parameter schema, step sequences, optional auto-retries and produces a signed recipe artifact. 2) Runtime executes recipes in a sandboxed container with enforced network and credential scopes and emits structured telemetry events to Ops Observability. 3) Console can render a recipe as an interactive shortflow (inputs, pre-checks, dry-run toggle). 4) Security review completed and KMS signing integrated. 5) Migration guide for converting two high-frequency support flows (DB failover and model cache flush) included.
implementation_notes: - DSL will be YAML-first with a compact JSON schema for validation. - Compile step will produce a recipe manifest + signature; verifier runs in the runtime prior to execution. - Execution runtime forks ephemeral worker with scoped secrets via short-lived tokens and sandboxed network policy. - Telemetry events follow the admin-run.events contract (event types: recipe.execute.request, recipe.step.start, recipe.step.complete, recipe.execute.result). - Provide SDK shims for Console (React) and opsctl (Go/CLI). - Feature-gate recipe execution behind 'admin_recipes.enabled' and quantify cost and latency before wide rollout. - Evaluate reuse of existing runbook parser from ENG-271888; avoid duplicate semantics.
